question.nlq: I would like to know which products have received a high number of complaints and list the total number of complaints for each of those products.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, the term high means the product has received at least five complaints.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(*) AS total_complaints
FROM Complaints c
JOIN Products p ON c.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, the term high means the product has received more complaints than the average number of complaints per product.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH complaint_counts AS (
    SELECT p.product_id,
           p.product_name,
           COUNT(c.complaint_id) AS total_complaints
    FROM Products p
    LEFT JOIN Complaints c ON p.product_id = c.product_id
    GROUP BY p.product_id
),
avg_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_complaints) AS avg_complaints
    FROM complaint_counts
)
SELECT cc.product_name, cc.total_complaints
FROM complaint_counts cc, avg_count a
WHERE cc.total_complaints > a.avg_complaints;

turns.text: What threshold should we use to define a 'high number' of complaints (e.g., more than 5 complaints per product)?
A product should be considered to have a high number of complaints if it has received at least five complaints.

WITH product_counts AS (
    SELECT p.product_id,
           p.product_name,
           COUNT(c.complaint_id) AS complaint_count
    FROM Products p
    LEFT JOIN Complaints c ON p.product_id = c.product_id
    GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
),
average_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(complaint_count) AS avg_cnt FROM product_counts
)
SELECT pc.product_id,
       pc.product_name,
       pc.complaint_count
FROM product_counts pc, average_count ac
WHERE pc.complaint_count > ac.avg_cnt
ORDER BY pc.complaint_count DESC;
